title: Modes of union: juxtaposition, coalescence, substance, relation
english: Union according to juxtaposition occurs with planks. Union according to coalescence occurs with a torch that proceeds from fire and is then united again. Union according to substance occurs with individuals, such as Peter and Paul, or certain horses, or oxen, or other animals. Union according to relation occurs with friends and opinions coming together into one will.

orientation: John of Damascus is listing the twelve modes of union with examples, and here he gives the examples for union according to juxtaposition, coalescence, substance, and relation.

title: Union according to composition and according to person
english: Union according to composition is seen in soul and body. Union according to person is spoken of only in the case of the divinity and humanity in Christ. For the two natures had one person, not two, contrary to the nonsense of Nestorius.

orientation: John of Damascus is listing the modes of union and now gives the mode according to composition, then the mode according to person, which he says applies only to Christ's divinity and humanity.

title: The union in Christ is essential, true, and preserves each nature's property
english: This kind of union is also called essential and true, not a matter of imagination.
Union according to person can also be defined another way: it is the coming together of things different in essence into one person, with the natural property of each being preserved after the union.
